root.label: First British Empire
root.gloss: How East India Company conquest, transatlantic slavery, Maroon resistance, and the American Revolution built and fractured empire.

children.label: Part 1: Company Rule in India
children.gloss: How London’s chartered East India Company transformed from coastal spice traders into the sovereign tax ruler of Mughal Bengal.

children.label: 1. East India Company & Bengal
children.q2Chain: 1600 Charter & Mughal Factories → Calcutta Clash & 1757 Plassey → 1765 Diwani & Bengal Famine
children.gloss: Causal Chain: 1600 Charter & Mughal Factories → Calcutta Clash & 1757 Plassey → 1765 Diwani & Bengal Famine.

children.label: 1600 Charter & Mughal Factories
children.gloss: Chartered by Elizabeth I in 1600, the Company won Mughal permission in 1615 to build fortified coastal factories guarded by sepoys.

children.label: 1600 Royal Monopoly Charter
children.gloss: 218 merchants pooled £68,000; Lancaster made 300% spice profit.

children.label: 1615 Roe & Jahangir Trade Decree
children.gloss: Built Surat and Calcutta depots; Fortified Madras and Bombay ports.

children.label: → Armed Sepoy Corporate Forts
children.gloss: Hired Indian infantry garrisons; Created armed coastal bridgeheads.

children.label: Calcutta Clash & 1757 Plassey
children.gloss: After Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah took Fort William in 1756, Robert Clive bribed Mir Jafar to win the June 1757 Battle of Plassey.

children.label: 1756 Fort William Cannon Dispute
children.gloss: Siraj marched 50,000 on Calcutta; Black Hole deaths stoked conquest.

children.label: 23 June 1757 Plassey Treachery
children.gloss: Clive bribed general Mir Jafar; Tarpaulins kept cannon powder dry.

children.label: → Installed Puppet Bengal Ruler
children.gloss: Routed Siraj’s soaked artillery; Handed Company political mastery.

children.label: 1765 Diwani & Bengal Famine
children.gloss: The 1765 Treaty of Allahabad granted the Company Bengal’s Diwani tax rights, fuelling corporate plunder and the 1770 famine.

children.label: 1765 Allahabad Diwani Treaty
children.gloss: Shah Alam II ceded land taxes; Ruled 20 million in Bengal.

children.label: Shah Alam II ceded land taxes
children.gloss: Shah Alam II ceded land taxes

children.label: → Worsened 1770 Bengal Famine
children.gloss: Relentless tax extraction in drought; Estimated ten million starved.

children.label: Merchants Became Sovereign State
children.gloss: Corporate profits soared in London; Laid base of British India.

children.label: Part 2: Slavery & Resistance
children.gloss: The triangular slave trade, Middle Passage atrocities, Jamaican Maroon guerrilla resistance under Queen Nanny, and 1807 abolition.

children.label: 2. Slave Trade & Middle Passage
children.q2Chain: Triangular Trade & RAC Monopoly → Middle Passage & Zong Massacre → Brookes, Equiano & 1807 Act
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Triangular Trade & RAC Monopoly → Middle Passage & Zong Massacre → Brookes, Equiano & 1807 Act.

children.label: Triangular Trade & RAC Monopoly
children.gloss: Liverpool and Bristol merchants linked manufactured goods, kidnapped Africans, and sugar, backed by the 1672 RAC and 1713 Asiento.

children.label: Guns, Captives & Raw Sugar Loop
children.gloss: Sailed from Liverpool and Bristol; Traded guns and brass for captives.

children.label: Traded guns and brass for captives
children.gloss: Traded guns and brass for captives

children.label: 1672 RAC & 1713 Spanish Asiento
children.gloss: Hot-iron RAC chest branding; Supplied Spanish American colonies.

children.label: → Made Britain Top Slave Trader
children.gloss: Enriched British ports and banks; Institutionalised royal trafficking.

children.label: Middle Passage & Zong Massacre
children.gloss: One in six captives died on chained Middle Passage crossings, culminating in the 1781 Zong insurance massacre of 133 people.

children.label: Eight-Week Chained Hold Crossing
children.gloss: Packed on suffocating wood shelves; One in six died at sea.

children.label: One in six died at sea
children.gloss: One in six died at sea

children.label: Nov 1781 Zong Ship Massacre
children.gloss: Collingwood drowned 133 captives; Claimed £30 per head insurance.

children.label: → Granville Sharp Exposed Trial
children.gloss: Judges treated lives as cargo; Shocked British public conscience.

children.label: Brookes, Equiano & 1807 Act
children.gloss: The Brookes ship diagram and Olaudah Equiano’s bestselling autobiography mobilized public pressure behind the 1807 Abolition Act.

children.label: Brookes Print & Equiano Memoir
children.gloss: Diagram showed stowed human holds; Equiano book recounted enslavement.

children.label: → Passed 1807 Abolition Act
children.gloss: Outlawed British slave trading; Followed mass national campaign.

children.label: Powered by African Testimony
children.gloss: Shattered pro-slavery myths; Left Caribbean slavery till 1833.

children.label: 3. Plantations & Queen Nanny
children.q2Chain: 1655 Jamaica & Sugar Brutality → Queen Nanny & First Maroon War → 1739 Maroon Peace Treaty
children.gloss: Causal Chain: 1655 Jamaica & Sugar Brutality → Queen Nanny & First Maroon War → 1739 Maroon Peace Treaty.

children.label: 1655 Jamaica & Sugar Brutality
children.gloss: Cromwell’s 1655 seizure of Jamaica birthed free mountain Maroon towns while coastal estates enforced lethal 18-hour sugar gangs.

children.label: 1655 Conquest & Maroon Towns
children.gloss: Cromwell seized Spanish Jamaica; Fugitives fortified Blue Mountains.

children.label: 18-Hour Sugar Cane Gang Regime
children.gloss: Driven by overseer cowhide whips; Iron mill rollers crushed hands.

children.label: → Daily Sabotage & Cultural Pride
children.gloss: Broke hoes and copper cauldrons; Kept Obeah and Anansi tales.

children.label: Queen Nanny & First Maroon War
children.gloss: Asante leader Queen Nanny trained Windward Maroons in branch camouflage and abeng horn ambushes, routing British regiments.

children.label: Branch Camouflage & Abeng Horns
children.gloss: Asante leader Queen Nanny led; Cow-horn signals guided ambushes.

children.label: → Routed Armed British Regiments
children.gloss: Held rugged mountain interior; Exhausted colonial militia forces.

children.label: Proved Armed Resistance Worked
children.gloss: Defended free African autonomy; Forced British truce flag.

children.label: 1739 Maroon Peace Treaty
children.gloss: Governor Trelawny recognized Maroon freedom and 1,500 sovereign acres in 1739, in exchange for returning future runaways.

children.label: Granted 1,500 Sovereign Acres
children.gloss: Governor Trelawny sent white flag; Guaranteed free Maroon self-rule.

children.label: → Required Returning Runaways
children.gloss: Pledged to catch future escapees; Protected lowland sugar estates.

children.label: Freedom Triumph vs Compromise
children.gloss: Humbled British imperial army; Forced painful runaway concession.

children.label: Part 3: American Revolution
children.gloss: Imperial war debt, unvoted taxes, the Boston Tea Party, 1776 Declaration, Yorktown, and the 1783 Black Loyalist exodus.

children.label: 4. Colonies & Boston Tea Party
children.q2Chain: 1763 Debt, Frontier & Stamp Act → 1770 Massacre & 1773 Tea Act → Boston Tea Party & Coercive Acts
children.gloss: Causal Chain: 1763 Debt, Frontier & Stamp Act → 1770 Massacre & 1773 Tea Act → Boston Tea Party & Coercive Acts.

children.label: 1763 Debt, Frontier & Stamp Act
children.gloss: Facing £133m war debt, Britain barred westward settlement in 1763 and passed the 1765 Stamp Act, sparking colonial boycotts.

children.label: £133m Debt & 1763 Frontier Line
children.gloss: Banned west Appalachian settling; Quartered 10,000 British soldiers.

children.label: 1765 Stamp Act & Boycott Riots
children.gloss: Taxed legal papers and cards; Sons of Liberty burned offices.

children.label: → 1766 Repeal & Representation Cry
children.gloss: Boycotts hurt British exporters; No tax without representation.

children.label: 1770 Massacre & 1773 Tea Act
children.gloss: Redcoats killed five in the 1770 Boston Massacre before the 1773 Tea Act granted the East India Company a colonial monopoly.

children.label: 5 March 1770 King Street Firing
children.gloss: Five killed with Crispus Attucks; Paul Revere print stoked fury.

children.label: May 1773 East India Tea Monopoly
children.gloss: 18m lb unsold tea in London; Bypassed local colonial traders.

children.label: → Sparked Seaport Tea Blockades
children.gloss: Feared unvoted tax precedent; Set stage for Griffin’s Wharf.

children.label: Boston Tea Party & Coercive Acts
children.gloss: Sons of Liberty dumped 342 tea chests into Boston Harbor in December 1773, provoking the punitive 1774 Coercive Acts.

children.label: 342 Tea Chests Smashed in Harbour
children.gloss: Mohawk-disguised Sons of Liberty; Dumped £10,000 tea in 3 hours.

children.label: → 1774 Coercive Acts Shut Port
children.gloss: George III closed Boston harbour; Suspended Massachusetts charter.

children.label: → Drove Thirteen Colonies to War
children.gloss: United colonies against coercion; Ignited April 1775 Lexington.

children.label: 5. 1776 Revolution & Loyalists
children.q2Chain: Lexington, Dunmore & 1776 Paradox → Saratoga, France & Yorktown → 1783 Paris & Black Loyalists
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Lexington, Dunmore & 1776 Paradox → Saratoga, France & Yorktown → 1783 Paris & Black Loyalists.

children.label: Lexington, Dunmore & 1776 Paradox
children.gloss: War erupted at Lexington in 1775 while Dunmore offered enslaved fighters freedom, exposing the hypocrisy of Jefferson’s 1776 text.

children.label: 1775 Lexington & Dunmore Offer
children.gloss: Minutemen fought Concord redcoats; Promised Black Loyalists freedom.

children.label: July 1776 Jefferson Declaration
children.gloss: Claimed all men created equal; 41 of 56 signers owned slaves.

children.label: Liberty Ideal vs Slavery Reality
children.gloss: Kept half a million enslaved; Ridiculed by Dr Samuel Johnson.

children.label: Saratoga, France & Yorktown
children.gloss: Saratoga brought France into a global naval war, culminating in Admiral de Grasse and Washington trapping Cornwallis at Yorktown.

children.label: Oct 1777 Saratoga Global Shift
children.gloss: Defeated General Burgoyne’s army; Louis XVI France joined rebels.

children.label: → Diverted Fleet to Sugar Islands
children.gloss: Defended lucrative West Indies; Stretched Royal Navy thin.

children.label: 19 Oct 1781 Yorktown Surrender
children.gloss: De Grasse blocked Chesapeake Bay; Cornwallis yielded 8,000 redcoats.

children.label: 1783 Paris & Black Loyalists
children.gloss: The 1783 Treaty of Paris recognized US independence while Sir Guy Carleton evacuated 3,000 Black Loyalists to Nova Scotia.

children.label: Sept 1783 Treaty of Paris
children.gloss: Recognized sovereign US republic; Ended First Atlantic Empire.

children.label: 3,000 Black Loyalists Evacuated
children.gloss: Carleton wrote Book of Negroes; Sailed to Nova Scotia & Freetown.

children.label: Shifted Empire Toward Asia
children.gloss: Pivoted expansion to India; Left US slavery entrenched.
